punchline: The same employees who hesitate to give up today's pay will agree to give up part of a raise that has not arrived yet.
thirty_sec: Economists Richard Thaler and Shlomo Benartzi asked employees to commit in advance to put part of every future raise into retirement saving, so nothing came out of today's pay. At the first company that tried it, 78 percent of those offered the plan joined and 80 percent of them stayed through the fourth raise. Their average saving rate went from 3.5 to 13.6 percent in 40 months.
